market_mood: Oil is back up as Iran-US diplomacy stalls, keeping diesel and jet fuel prices elevated, while tech rallies on SpaceX earnings, Super Micro's raised guidance and Musk's Tesla-SpaceX merger talk. Deal flow stays heavy in healthcare and data-center services.
self_check: My high-confidence calls have been the weakest part of the record (2 of 11), especially chasing oil names right after a price spike, while geopolitics and merger ideas have worked best. Today I kept conviction more measured, leaned on second-order energy effects rather than the crude spike itself, and avoided crowded AI headlines.

picks.reason: Washington is coaxing refiners to make more diesel and is lending out heating oil reserves because distillate prices are surging, and analysts say diesel stays high; refining margins are the direct beneficiary.
The FAA finally certified the 737 Max 10 after six years of delays, unlocking deliveries of the largest Max model and the cash that comes with them.

Cencora is buying American Oncology Network for $2.4B, deepening its high-margin community oncology services; acquirer moves on this kind of bolt-on often get digested over weeks rather than instantly.
United just cut its 2026 profit outlook purely on fuel costs, and oil jumped another $2 as Iran diplomacy stalled, so the same jet-fuel squeeze should pressure peers.
Broadcast TV is set to take nearly half of record midterm political ad spending, and local-station owners like Nexstar are the main collectors of that cash in the next two weeks.
CBRE is buying Onnec for up to about $1B to expand data-center infrastructure services, giving it a bigger slice of the AI buildout that the market still values as a property broker.

No major news today beyond commentary on whether cloud profits can fund its Zoox robotaxi bet.

Reports third-quarter results after the close tonight; the debate is AI capex versus ad revenue growth.
Up on Musk confirming board committees exploring a SpaceX merger, with earnings also due after the bell.
In the news for facilitating a Syrian deal for Saudi oil products; broader focus is next week's Fed decision.

Hot UK inflation and talk of further rate hikes abroad keep upward pressure on long yields, a headwind for bond prices.

top_buys.pitch: Distillate shortage is a refiner's windfall and Washington is openly asking for more diesel.
top_buys.why: US officials are coaxing refiners to raise diesel output and plan to lend out roughly a third of the heating oil reserve because prices are surging, which tells you how tight distillate is. Reuters also reports diesel is expected to stay high despite the Russia deal. HF Sinclair is a mid-cap refiner with heavy distillate exposure that tends to lag the larger names on the initial headline.
top_buys.risks: A sudden Iran or Ukraine diplomatic breakthrough could crack crack spreads quickly, and refiners are volatile on inventory data.
top_buys.watch: Weekly EIA distillate inventories and refiner earnings guidance in the next two weeks.

top_buys.pitch: The 737 Max 10 is finally certified after six years of delays.
top_buys.why: FAA approval removes a long-running overhang and lets Boeing start delivering its largest narrowbody, which converts a big backlog of parked airframes into customer cash. Certifications like this get a one-day headline but the delivery ramp and associated cash flow improvement unfold over quarters. Airlines facing high fuel costs also want the more efficient Max 10.
top_buys.risks: Boeing has repeatedly missed production ramp targets, and any new quality issue would reverse sentiment fast.
top_buys.watch: Monthly delivery numbers and the first Max 10 handover date.

top_buys.pitch: United's fuel-driven guidance cut is a template for the rest of the industry.
top_buys.why: United slashed its 2026 profit outlook specifically because fuel keeps climbing, and crude jumped another $2 overnight as Iran rejected diplomatic progress. Jet fuel is made from the same distillate pool that is already critically tight, so the squeeze is worse than headline crude suggests. Investors often treat one airline's warning as company-specific before the read-across sinks in.
top_buys.risks: Demand is holding up and fares are rising, so strong bookings could offset fuel; a peace headline would send oil down fast.
top_buys.watch: Delta's next investor update and weekly jet-fuel crack spreads.

top_buys.pitch: A $2.4B oncology acquisition pushes Cencora further into higher-margin specialty care.
top_buys.why: Buying American Oncology Network expands Cencora's community oncology platform, which carries better economics than core drug distribution. Health care has been one of the stronger sectors over the past week, giving the idea a tailwind. Acquirer re-ratings on strategic bolt-ons typically play out over weeks as analysts update models.
top_buys.risks: Deals of this size can dilute near-term earnings, and payer reimbursement pressure in oncology is a real risk.
top_buys.watch: Management commentary on accretion at the next quarterly report.

top_buys.pitch: Record midterm ad spending, and nearly half of it still goes to broadcast TV.
top_buys.why: CNBC reports broadcast stations will capture close to half of political ad dollars in a record midterm cycle, and Nexstar is the largest pure-play local station group. Polling showing a tight, contentious race environment means more money dumped into swing-state airwaves in the final two weeks. The market often underrates how concentrated this revenue is in the final stretch.
top_buys.risks: Political ad revenue is one-off and secular cord-cutting keeps pressuring the core business; the stock can sell off right after the election.
top_buys.watch: Election-day results and Nexstar's Q4 political revenue commentary.

summary.big_story: Stalled Iran-US diplomacy pushed oil up $2 and kept diesel prices surging, while tech rallied on SpaceX earnings and Super Micro's raised guidance.
summary.top_pick: HF Sinclair, because surging diesel margins and a US government push for more distillate output land straight on refiners' profits.
summary.watch: Meta and Tesla earnings after the close, plus any movement in Iran-US or Ukraine diplomacy that could reverse the oil move.
